transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Julia Park (CTO, Seabright), Ethan Cole (Head of Infrastructure), Nina Rosas (Security Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Seabright is evaluating Redwood for inference hosting across hosted and dedicated initially; private deployment is a gating item if data residency and on-prem rules apply.
- Key compliance asks: SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 alignment, SSO via SAML, RBAC scoping, audit log retention 7 years, and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) preferred for production.

Topics: SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, data retention, hosted/dedicated/private, benchmarks

[00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intro, I'm Aisha, I'm the account lead on this. Marco's our solutions engineer, Priya's on customer success. How are we all?
[00:12] Julia (Seabright CTO): Hi; thanks. We're excited to get an initial sense of how Redwood would fit into our stack.
[00:18] Marco (Redwood SE): Great — we'll try to keep this very practical: security posture, what you need, and then walk through deployment options.
[00:28] Ethan (Head Infra): Quick note — we've got some regulatory constraints, so data residency and KMS are big ones for us.
[00:35] Nina (Security Eng): Yep, and our InfoSec team wants to see SOC2 evidence and log retention details.
[00:40] Aisha: Perfect. Before we dive: are you leaning hosted first or are you already expecting to go dedicated/private?
[00:48] Julia: We're thinking hosted for an internal pilot, but for production we may need dedicated or private depending on the KMS/residency answers.
[00:56] Marco: Makes sense. For hosted we can provide encryption in transit and at rest, and we offer a customer-managed KMS integration in our Dedicated and Private tiers — small clarification: with Hosted we support BYOK via cloud KMS for some regions, but full HSM-managed keys are available on Private.
[01:18] Nina: When you say BYOK — do you rotate keys? Do you provide key access logs? Our auditors will ask.
[01:26] Marco: Yeah, we log key usage events; we can show audit logs for KMS operations. On Dedicated we can point logs to your SIEM or S3 bucket. There might be minor differences in the log schema between Hosted and Dedicated but the entries are there — times, action, principal.
[01:48] Ethan: How about SSO? We use SAML with our IdP and need SCIM for user sync.
[01:54] Priya (Redwood CSM): We support SSO via SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning; RBAC maps to groups from the IdP. There's an admin role mapping and you can define custom roles via the Console.
[02:08] Julia: Are those console role changes auditable? We need change history for admin changes.
[02:13] Marco: Yes — audit trails include role changes, logins, API key creation and revocation. Retention is configurable; by default it's 90 days for Hosted, but for enterprise plans we can extend log retention and ship logs to your storage for long-term archival.
[02:34] Nina: We're aiming for 7 years retention for certain logs — is that feasible?
[02:38] Marco: Absolutely — in Dedicated/Private we generally recommend shipping logs to your storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) and from there you manage retention policy. For Hosted we can provide longer retention as an add-on but it usually goes through a contract.
[02:56] Aisha: On compliance: we have a SOC2 Type II attestation and an ISO 27001 binder for platform controls; happy to share those.
[03:04] Julia: That would be helpful. Also, do you have third-party penetration test reports or summary?
[03:09] Marco: We have a pen test summary and a whitebox results summary — will include redacted findings. We'll send those alongside SOC2.
[03:18] Ethan: For private deployments — what's the runtime footprint? If we host on-prem we might need GPUs in our datacenters.
[03:26] Marco: Our Private package is flexible: we ship a control plane you run in your VPC, or an on-prem installer for air-gapped environments. The runtime requires CUDA-enabled GPUs for larger models; for smaller model variants you can run on T4/A10s. We'll share recommended instance counts based on your expected qps.
[03:45] Nina: Important to ask: key separation. If we use Redwood-managed KMS in hosted, do Redwood operators have any access to customer keys?
[03:52] Marco: No operator access to keys. For Hosted BYOK we use enveloping — the master key is customer-controlled in their cloud KMS. For Dedicated we can also support customer KMS in your cloud, and for Private you keep full control.
[04:08] Julia: Auditability: can we get a sample of the audit logs schema?
[04:12] Marco: Yes, we'll attach a sample JSON schema of logs. Note there are fields like request_id, model_variant, token_count, principal, ip, and action.
[04:25] Ethan: About data retention: do you store prompt/response by default? We prefer ephemeral tokens only, but need some traces for debugging.
[04:34] Priya: By default we store request metadata for 30 days for customer support purposes; content retention is configurable. For enterprise customers you can opt out of storing full request payloads or route content to your logs only.
[04:47] Nina: For PII, what's the recommended approach? We want to redact at client side but also ensure logs don't keep unredacted content.
[04:55] Marco: We recommend client-side redaction and then storing only hashes or metadata. If you need, we can enable automatic redaction patterns for known PII types, but that's more of a product feature and we can enable it in Dedicated/Private environments with additional config.
[05:14] Julia: On SLA — what's uptime for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[05:18] Aisha: Hosted is a managed SLA depending on plan; Dedicated comes with an enterprise SLA (99.9%+ typical) since you have reserved hardware and fallbacks. Private SLAs are agreed in the contract.
[05:26] Ethan: For throughput and latency — can you share per-token latencies for the model families?
[05:31] Marco: We'll send benchmark sheets. For a 4k context model on A100s we're typically sub-50ms per-token at steady state with batching; with smaller GPUs or different quantization you'll see variance. We'll include typical quantization/throughput tradeoffs in the doc.
[05:50] Nina: Any concerns about data egress? We're in EU and need to keep data in-region for some workloads.
[05:57] Marco: Regions matter — we have hosted endpoints in EU regions and can pin requests to EU-only infra. For Dedicated/Private you can keep everything in your VPC/region.
[06:08] Julia: On RBAC and admin separation — we need separation between tenant admins and infra ops. Can RBAC be scoped to teams and projects?
[06:16] Priya: Yes — roles can be scoped at org, project, and route levels. You can also create service accounts with restricted scopes.
[06:24] Ethan: If we rotate service account keys, how long are old tokens valid? We need immediate revocation.
[06:29] Marco: API keys can be revoked immediately; we also support short-lived tokens via our auth flow.
[06:35] Nina: For forensic readiness — do you capture request and response hashes, and can you provide a timeline if there's an incident?
[06:44] Marco: We capture request_id and metadata by default; content can be excluded. We can provide timeline exports and integrate with your SIEM for alerts.
[06:54] Julia: Let's talk SAML specifics — our IdP uses signed assertions and requires audience restrictions and encrypted assertions. Any limitations?
[07:02] Marco: We support signed assertions and audience restrictions; encrypted assertions are supported in Dedicated/Private setups. For Hosted we'll need to confirm with your IdP specifics — sometimes encrypted assertions add complexity to SP integration.
[07:16] Nina: SCIM provisioning: can we auto-provision groups and map to RBAC roles?
[07:21] Priya: Yes, group-to-role mapping is supported. We'll share our SCIM doc.
[07:27] Ethan: On audit log retention again — shipping logs to our S3 seems the cleanest. Any PII concerns with shipping logs out of hosted?
[07:34] Marco: If you route logs to your bucket in your cloud account (preferred), Redwood does not persist those copies. For Hosted we can set up a delivery pipeline to your account — that satisfies residency and retention.
[07:46] Aisha: Quick question from legal: do you have a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) or standard contract language for data residency?
[07:52] Marco: Yes — standard DPA and addenda for regional controls. We'll attach a template.
[07:59] Julia: Any red flags on your side for us to be aware of as we think about timeline?
[08:05] Aisha: Not really — mostly documentation and a short benchmark to validate latency and cost. If you require Private for production that adds lead time for infra deployment.
[08:14] Ethan: Lead time — how long to spin up Dedicated capacity?
[08:18] Marco: Usually 2-6 weeks depending on region and capacity; Private on-prem can be longer (4-12 weeks) depending on hardware procurement.
[08:28] Nina: Would you allow us to run a short PoC where we only send synthetic data to avoid PII leakage?
[08:33] Aisha: Definitely — we encourage synthetic data for initial benchmarks. We'll provide a test account.
[08:39] Julia: Pricing — can you ballpark monthly reserved cost for a small Dedicated pool?
[08:44] Marco: We'll include a sample: e.g., 2x A100 reserved might be $Xk/month — we'll send concrete pricing in the follow-up.
[08:53] Ethan: Regarding tracing — can we instrument request traces across our infra into Redwood's traces?
[08:59] Marco: We have tracing hooks and a request_id that you can include in your logs. We also support OTLP export for traces into your observability stack on Dedicated & Private.
[09:11] Nina: On legal/regulatory: ISO 27001 certificate?
[09:15] Marco: We maintain ISO alignment; we'll provide certificate copies and scope.
[09:20] Priya: I'll follow up with a doc bundle containing SOC2, ISO, pen test summary, SCIM/SAML guides, sample audit log schema, and a small benchmark plan.
[09:30] Julia: That would be perfect.
[09:33] Aisha: Great — recap in short: Redwood to send compliance pack + sample logs + Dedicated pricing + test account. Seabright to share retention policy and confirm which pilot region to use.
[09:47] Ethan: We'll try to pick pilot region EU-west-1 and confirm by Friday.
[09:52] Nina: I'll also prep a redacted data sample for the benchmark.
[09:57] Marco: Sound good — we'll propose 2026-12-15 for the technical deep dive.
[10:03] Julia: Works for us.
[10:05] Aisha: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up over email with the attachments.
[10:10] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some names and acronyms may be imperfectly transcribed (e.g., HSM/ASM, K-V cache spelled as KV cache or K-V, SAML sometimes S-A-M-L). There is occasional crosstalk.
